column7: Original three-control fuzz using a mixture of NOS germanium and modern silicon transistors; Focus control moves the circuit from lower-gain distortion-like response toward thicker, more aggressive fuzz. Custom sheet-steel enclosure with silver hammertone finish. Limited to 250 units worldwide due to transistor availability.
column10: Strong first-edition identifiers: Focus/Level/Fuzz control set, hybrid Ge/Si construction, 250-unit limit and hammertone enclosure.

column7: After the original 250-unit Focus Fuzz sold out, Great Eastern launched an all-silicon, all-original version in July 2023. It is a darker/grittier and more affordable design using selected low-gain silicon transistors; 3-control interface retained, with pedalboard-friendly compact enclosure.
column10: Treat Silicon as a distinct product variant/generation-state rather than an artwork edition. External identification centers on silicon-specific labeling/specification and the post-sellout launch.

column7: All-analog upper-octave pedal reworking and improving the Shriek circuit from the MOAI MAEA; discrete transistor fuzz, enhanced rectification, pre-gain second-order low-pass filter, separate Dry and OCT+ mixing, Timbre and Filter controls, top-mounted jacks and relay soft switching.
column10: Distinctive four-control surface and top-jack layout, plus the explicit Shriek/MOAI MAEA lineage, are high-value identification markers.

column7: Latest installment in the Dr Freakenstein dynasty; retains the core massive gated fuzz used across earlier Dr Freakenstein versions but adds Overtone, LFO and Chop sections, Igor pressure controller, CV control, Hi/Lo switch and eye meter. Compact custom enclosure; true bypass.
column10: Preserve the dynasty lineage without collapsing prior Chop Fuzz and Chop Fuzzz identities. The three-Z spelling is itself a useful external clue because Rainger says it distinguishes this from the previous Chop Fuzz.

column7: Octafuzz designed as a versatile standalone pedal rather than a one-trick genre device; current builder documentation identifies Volume, Tone and Gain controls plus two toggles for dual voicing and symmetrical/asymmetrical clipping. NOS edition exists as a separate edition.
column10: 2023 GPX coverage places the Octaurus in the new-pedal census. Primary historical launch documentation and exact introduction date still need enrichment.

column7: Germanium/silicon hybrid fuzz with three controls: Gain, Tone and Level. Tone functions as bass reduction, input impedance is moderately low, and the pedal uses a NOS germanium transistor, all-analog signal path and relay true-bypass soft switching. Built and hand-wired in Portland, Oregon.
column10: 2023 GPX coverage identifies Charon as a Ge/Si hybrid fuzz. Current Spaceman documentation also establishes a later Charon v2 Mod as a reworked take, so the original must remain a separate identity.
